description: Read one whole card by its `id`, or by its `set` and the number printed on it, `localId` — not both. The set may be an id or a printed name, ignoring case, and leading zeros in the number are optional. Returns the shape search_cards gives at `detail` 'full'. A card that does not exist is an error saying whether the set or the number was wrong.

id.description: Global card id, e.g. 'swsh3-136'. Give it alone; take it from a search_cards or get_set result rather than composing one.

language.description: Catalogue language. Names, values and set lists are localised (the Asian catalogues have their own set ids), so look values up in it; prices are the same in every language.

localId.description: The number printed on the card, e.g. '105'; leading zeros are optional. Give it with `set`, not with `id`.

set.description: The card's set, given with `localId`: id ('sv04.5') or printed name ('Paldean Fates'), ignoring case; a name several sets share covers them all. list_sets lists both.

name: get_card

card.description: The whole card, in the requested language: every field you can search on, its rules text (attacks, abilities and effect), its weaknesses and resistances, its tournament legality and its image URLs. Market prices are not part of it — call get_card_pricing for those. Per-variant print details, physical attributes and flavour text are deliberately omitted. A field being absent means the card has no such value, not that the lookup failed.

abilities.description: The card's abilities. Pokemon cards only, and most Pokemon cards have none.

effect.description: The ability's printed effect text. Can be absent in a language whose catalogue is incompletely translated.

name.description: The ability's printed name. Can be absent in a language whose catalogue is incompletely translated.

type.description: The kind of ability, e.g. 'Ability' or 'Poke-POWER'.

attacks.description: The card's attacks. Pokemon cards only.

cost.description: The energy required, one entry per energy symbol printed — two Fire symbols appear as two Fire entries. Absent when the catalogue records no cost, which is sometimes a genuinely free attack but often a gap in its data, so do not read absence as free.

damage.description: The damage the attack deals, as printed and always as text: '30' for a fixed amount, or a conditional amount such as '60+', '20×' or '20-', where the effect text decides the rest — the modifier is always written '+', '-' or '×', whichever glyph the catalogue used. Absent when it deals none, such as an attack that only draws cards.

effect.description: The attack's printed effect text. Absent when the attack only deals damage.

name.description: The attack's printed name. Can be absent in a language whose catalogue is incompletely translated.

category.description: The top-level kind of card, which governs what else is present: only Pokemon cards carry hp, types, stage, attacks, weaknesses, resistances, dexId, evolveFrom and description; only Trainer cards carry trainerType; only Energy cards carry energyType.

dexId.description: The National Pokedex numbers of the Pokemon depicted. Pokemon cards only, and an array because one card can depict several.

effect.description: The card's printed effect text. Trainer and Energy cards only — a Pokemon card's text lives on its attacks and abilities instead.

energyType.description: Whether an Energy card is Normal or Special. Energy cards only.

evolveFrom.description: The name of the Pokemon this one evolves from. Pokemon cards only, and absent on Basic Pokemon.

hp.description: The card's printed hit points. Pokemon cards only.

id.description: The card's globally unique id, formed from its set id and its number within that set, e.g. 'swsh3-136'. The only value here that identifies a card on its own, and the value get_card's 'id' form takes.

illustrator.description: The artist credited on the card. Absent on roughly half of all cards, particularly older ones.

images.description: Ready-to-use webp URLs for the card face, which resolve as given. Absent for roughly one card in ten, which is ordinary upstream data rather than a failed lookup.

high.description: A full-resolution rendering, legible enough to read the card's printed text.

low.description: A smaller rendering, enough to recognise the card by.

legal.description: Tournament legality, covering the standard and expanded formats only. Every card is legal in unlimited play, so both being false does not mean the card is unplayable. Absent on a Pokémon TCG Pocket card, to which the Trading Card Game's formats do not apply.

localId.description: The number printed on the card face. Unique only within a set — many sets have a card '1' — so it identifies a card only alongside 'set', which is the pair get_card's second form takes. A string rather than a number because some cards are numbered with letters or symbols, e.g. '!'.

name.description: The card's printed name, including any suffix next to it. Not unique: the same name recurs across sets and sometimes within one, which is why 'set' and 'localId' are needed to tell two results apart.

platform.description: Whether this is a physically printed Trading Card Game card or exists only in the digital game Pokémon TCG Pocket. A Pocket card was never printed, so it carries no regulation mark and no 'legal' at all, because the Trading Card Game's formats do not apply to it. It is not distinguishable by its images, which Pocket cards do have.

anyOf.description: A rarity as the catalogue spells it.
The card was printed with no rarity symbol, which the catalogue spells 'None'.

rarity.description: The print rarity as the catalogue spells it. Names vary across eras, so two similarly scarce cards may not share one. Null for a card printed with no rarity symbol, such as a promo or a starter-deck card: the catalogue's own value for that is 'None', which is what the rarity filter takes to find them. Absent when the catalogue records no rarity at all — over half of Traditional Chinese cards — so absence is not the same as null.

regulationMark.description: The regulation mark letter governing tournament legality, in upper case. Only cards from the Sword & Shield era onward carry one.

resistances.description: The types this Pokemon takes reduced damage from. Pokemon cards only.

type.description: The energy type the resistance applies to.

value.description: The modifier as printed, e.g. '-20'. A string, not a number.

retreat.description: The card's retreat cost in energy, where 0 means the card retreats for free. Pokemon cards only. Absent means the catalogue records no cost at all for it, which is a gap in its data rather than a free retreat, and does not distinguish that from a non-Pokemon card either — read 'category' for that.

set.description: The set this card belongs to. Only its id and name are carried; call get_set or list_sets for its size and platform.

id.description: The set's id, which is also the value the 'set' filter takes, e.g. 'swsh3'.

name.description: The set's printed name, which the 'set' filter also accepts, e.g. 'Darkness Ablaze'.

stage.description: The Pokemon's evolution stage, e.g. 'Basic' or 'Stage1'. Pokemon cards only.

suffix.description: The suffix printed next to the card's name, e.g. 'EX' or 'V'. Most cards have none. Pokémon TCG Pocket's ex cards carry 'EX' here, as upstream records them, though the printed game's 'EX' and 'ex' are different mechanics.

trainerType.description: The subtype of a Trainer card, e.g. 'Item' or 'Supporter'. Trainer cards only.

types.description: The card's elemental types. Pokemon cards only, and usually one, though dual-type cards exist.

variants.description: Which printings of this card were produced. A flag being true means such a printing exists, not that this result is that printing.

firstEdition.description: A first-edition printing exists, carrying the first-edition stamp.

holo.description: A holo printing exists, where the artwork itself is foiled.

reverse.description: A reverse-holo printing exists, where the card body is foiled rather than the artwork.

weaknesses.description: The types this Pokemon takes extra damage from. Pokemon cards only.

type.description: The energy type the weakness applies to.

value.description: The modifier as printed, e.g. '×2'. A string, not a number.

language.description: The catalogue language this response was read in.
